item.title: Kuma River Rafting — Guide
item.description: The Kuma River, flowing through the Hitoyoshi valley in the mountains near the Kagoshima–Kumamoto border, is renowned as one of the three fastest-flowing rivers in Japan, making it a premier destination for river adventure. Its lively rapids and clear waters, set amid green mountains, are ideal for exhilarating white-water rafting trips in the warmer months, with guided tours suitable for beginners, families and thrill-seekers who paddle together through the rapids and calmer pools.

item.title: Naniwa Yodogawa Fireworks: Osaka's Great Summer Hanabi — Guide
item.description: The Naniwa Yodogawa Fireworks Festival is one of the biggest and best-loved summer events in Osaka, staged on a single night in high summer over the broad Yodogawa river in the north of the city. Run largely on public donations, it sends tens of thousands of shells into the sky in a tightly choreographed programme, the wide river giving space for huge low bursts reflected in the water and a finale that fills the whole sky.

item.title: Niyodogawa River: The Famous 'Niyodo Blue' — Guide
item.description: The Niyodogawa is one of Japan’s clearest rivers, celebrated for a colour so vivid it has its own name: ‘Niyodo Blue’, a luminous turquoise that glows in the sunlight where the water runs deep and pure over pale stones. Flowing from the mountains of central Kochi, it is dotted with jewel-like spots — the pool beneath Nakatsu Gorge, the astonishing clarity of Niko-buchi pool, waterfalls and swimming holes framed by forested slopes.

item.title: River Kayaking & Canoeing in Miyazaki — Guide
item.description: Miyazaki’s mountainous interior is laced with beautiful, clear rivers that make superb settings for kayaking and canoeing. On the scenic Gokase River near Takachiho and other inland waterways, guided tours let paddlers glide across calm, emerald-green stretches of water framed by forested gorges, cliffs and greenery, taking in the pristine scenery from the water at a gentle pace. Suitable for beginners, families and experienced paddlers alike, the tours typically provide all equipment and a guide, and range from relaxing flat-water paddles on rivers and reservoirs to more adventurous stretches.

item.title: River Kayaking and Canyoning in Saga — Guide
item.description: For an active, adventurous side of Saga, the rivers and gorges of the mountainous south offer kayaking and canyoning. Guided kayak tours let you paddle across calm rivers and reservoirs among forested hills, gliding on clear water and taking in the peaceful scenery at your own pace — suitable for beginners with a guide. For more of a thrill, canyoning (or ‘shower climbing’) tours take you into the mountain gorges to scramble, wade, slide down natural rock chutes and jump into clear pools beneath waterfalls, wearing a wetsuit and helmet — a wet, exhilarating way to experience the wild river landscape.
